data.title: Nvidia (NVDA) Could Invest $2 Billion in Nscale Ahead of $3 Billion IPO
data.description:
AI cloud company Nscale is reportedly seeking as much as $3.5 billion in private financing ahead of a planned IPO that could raise another $3 billion. According to Bloomberg, which cited people familiar with the matter, the London-based company wants to sell up to $1.5 billion of convertible notes and is also seeking about $2 billion from chipmaker Nvidia (NVDA). The fundraising comes as Nscale tells investors that it has about $103 billion of contracted business after signing a $45 billion computing agreement with Anthropic.

The convertible-note round is expected to be led by Daniel Loeb's Third Point, while investment bank Goldman Sachs (GS) is working on the fundraising. For reference, convertible notes start as debt and can later turn into shares. As a result, participating investors could eventually own part of Nscale after it goes public.

Nscale is offering the notes at a double-digit discount to the eventual IPO price. That discount can adjust until the company reaches a $30 billion valuation. Above that level, the conversion price would remain fixed.

Promotion

Nscale Is Funding a Huge AI Infrastructure Expansion

Nscale has told investors that its contracts could support about $18.1 billion in annual revenue and roughly $13.6 billion in adjusted EBITDA. However, the company said that those estimates are only examples and should not be treated as formal guidance.

A major part of that potential business comes from Anthropic, which agreed to pay Nscale $45 billion for computing capacity. Nscale is also developing a large data center campus in Norway that will serve tech giant Microsoft (MSFT). Another major campus is planned in West Virginia.

Unsurprisingly, the company's hardware needs are enormous. Most of its active chips are Nvidia Blackwell GPUs, and Nscale has contracted for about 194,000 Nvidia Vera Rubin GPUs.

Nscale is also expanding into robotics. It recently agreed to provide Figure with at least $3.5 billion of computing capacity and plans to become a shareholder in the robotics startup. In July, Nscale also agreed to buy AI software company Anyscale for $1.65 billion.

data.title: $200 per Share? Intel Stock (NASDAQ:INTC) Gains With New Projections
data.description:
Chip stock Intel (INTC) was the beneficiary of a new report out from Global Equities Research analyst Trip Chowdhry, who has a four-star rating on TipRanks. Chowdhry believes that the recent earnings report out from Dell Technologies (DELL) could be a huge win for Intel. Investors seemed to agree, and Intel shares rose over 3% in Friday afternoon's trading. Intel has seen a 274.32% rally in its share price over the past year.

Yeah, But How?

The idea that Intel could nearly double from what it is today, potentially reaching $200 per share, may sound strange, but Chowdhry has an unexpected impetus for that: surging artificial intelligence (AI) workloads. Basically, the report that Dell's server revenue was up 122% in a year-to-year comparison was a good sign that Intel's CPUs are poised for some big new sales. In fact, Chowdhry was projecting 16-fold year-over-year growth at one point. While Intel does have plenty of competition in this space, its name recognition in the field will help, and the market will be sufficiently large that this rising tide will likely lift every boat.

Complete Commitment

United States Senator Bernie Moreno did not think much of Intel's plans to bring a foundry to New Albany in Ohio. In fact, back in September 2025, Moreno sent a letter to Intel's CEO Lip-Bu Tan, asking if the plant was ever actually going in. Considering that Moreno's letter included words like "fraud" and "charade," this could have been a problem. But subsequent word from Tan turned things around, and now, Senator Moreno is much more confident that Intel will get the plant up and running after all.

data.title: Why Is the Stock Market Down Today, 9/4/26?
data.description:
Both the S&P 500 (SPX) and the Nasdaq 100 (NDX) are trading lower on Friday. The S&P 500 is down 0.52%, while the Nasdaq 100 is off 0.12%. Higher interest rate expectations continue to weigh on the market, with the odds of a 25-basis-point rate hike on September 16 rising to 58.4% compared to 49.4% yesterday and 57% a week ago.

The odds received a boost after the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) announced this morning that nonfarm payrolls climbed 162,000 in August, nearly tripling the consensus estimate of 55,000. The Fed is less incentivized to cut rates when job growth is strong and has more flexibility to focus on inflation, which has remained above the central bank's 2% target for 65 consecutive months. Higher rates can ease price pressures by increasing borrowing costs and discouraging spending.

Stock Market Slips on Trump's Trade Warnings and Tech Weakness

Following the jobs report, President Trump threatened to eliminate trade with countries with which the U.S. has a deficit unless the Fed cuts rates. He also said that the "fear of inflation" is holding back economic growth and the stock market.

data.title: 'Fear of Inflation' Is Killing Economic Growth, Trump Says
data.description:
President Trump said Friday that August's job report should be sending the stock market higher. Instead, the market is in the red because the "fear of inflation" is dragging down economic growth and the S&P 500 (SPX).

The Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) announced this morning that nonfarm payrolls increased by 162,000 in August, shattering expectations of 55,000. However, the data sent equities lower, as a healthy labor market allows the Fed to focus on inflation, the other aspect of its dual mandate. Inflation has remained above the Fed's 2% target for 65 consecutive months. Higher interest rates can help ease inflation but also pressure stocks by raising borrowing costs and lowering the present value of future cash flows.

Trump Presses Fed as Rate Hike Odds Rise

Trump added that the U.S. should have the lowest rates in the world, pointing out that every basis point of higher rates costs the U.S. $650 billion per year in debt payments. "We should pay the Lowest Interest Rates in the World because we make everything run, and give otherwise failed countries Great Economic Wealth!" he said in a Truth Social post.

data.title: Apple Stock: Citi Sees 7.3 Million Foldable iPhone Sales Despite $2,000 Price
data.description:
Tech giant Apple (AAPL) could charge more than $2,000 for its first foldable iPhone, according to Citi (C) analysts led by five-star-rated Asiya Merchant, who is ranked #8 out of 12,498 Wall Street analysts. Interestingly, though, analysts still expect millions of customers to buy it. Citi estimates that the device, which could be called the iPhone Ultra, will sell about 5 million units in the second half of 2026. Another 2.3 million could follow in the first quarter of 2027. That would put early sales at roughly 7.3 million units as Apple prepares for its September 9 "Surprise and Shine" event under new CEO John Ternus.

That premium price could also help Apple deal with the rising cost of memory chips. Indeed, Apple recently gave cautious revenue guidance partly because it cannot secure enough memory to meet demand. Higher memory prices also pressured margins last quarter.

Notably, former CEO Tim Cook described the situation as a "100-year flood" during his final earnings call. He said that Apple had reluctantly raised prices because memory costs had increased dramatically.

Unsurprisingly, the pricing pressure is coming from the AI boom. High-end memory used in AI servers is in short supply because demand continues to exceed available capacity. In fact, Memory maker SK Hynix (SKHY) has largely sold out much of its premium AI memory capacity for 2026.

At the same time, AI chipmakers like Nvidia (NVDA) need large amounts of advanced memory for their systems, while cloud giants like Microsoft (MSFT) and Amazon (AMZN) are spending heavily on AI infrastructure. To make matters worse, industry experts currently expect supply to remain tight into 2027.

As a result, memory suppliers have gained more pricing power, and customers such as Apple face higher costs.

data.title: Boeing Stock (NYSE:BA) Slips as the Spirit AeroSystems Deal Starts Looking Bad
data.description:
Aerospace stock Boeing (BA) recently bought Spirit AeroSystems in a bid to handle some of Boeing's supply chain issues. But the purchase has delivered some issues along with it, and it turns out that Boeing's new buy is a bit of a money pit. Investors seemed concerned as well, and Boeing shares are down fractionally in Friday afternoon's trading. Boeing has seen an 8.32% loss in its share price over the past year.

Lost the Spirit

Boeing paid a hefty $8.4 billion to buy Spirit back in December, and in so doing brought a big part of its fuselage processing under its own umbrella. But it turns out that Spirit had more problems than even Boeing expected, discovering what a Wall Street Journal report called "…hundreds of millions of dollars in additional liabilities…beyond what it initially recognized after the deal closed."

The good news, thanks to accounting rules, is that these issues do not appear on Boeing's income statements. Rather, they are a part of footnotes about the Spirit acquisition. But the losses are no less real, bringing greater costs to Boeing on unfavorable contracts. It also represents "…yet another headwind" for investors, the report noted.

data.title: Why Cerebras Stock (CBRS) Is Soaring Today — Sept. 4, 2026
data.description:
Shares in U.S. chipmaker Cerebras Systems (CBRS) climbed by more than 12% to around $214 on Friday afternoon. This came amid a rally in AI chip stocks and a sentiment boost triggered by Nvidia's (NVDA) roughly $13 billion acquisition deal for Hugging Face. Notably, CBRS has also closed higher over the past two days after the company announced a new AI data center in Mikkeli, Finland.

Cerebras Stock Joins AI Chip Stock Rally

For context, Cerebras is an AI infrastructure company. It builds the world's largest computer chips called the Wafer-Scale Engine (WSE). The company creates single, giant processors the size of an entire silicon wafer to speed up AI training and applications.

Cerebras shares joined the chip-stock rally on Friday. The rally came as analysts hailed Nvidia's plan to acquire Hugging Face, an open-source platform used for AI development.

data.title: Memory Stocks Micron (MU) and SanDisk (SNDK) Have Big Upside Potential, Says Lynx Research
data.description:
Lynx Research is bullish on the memory sector, assigning aggressive price targets of $1,325 for Micron (MU) and $2,450 for SanDisk (SNDK). Based on current prices of $1,006 and $1,727, those targets imply 31.7% and 41.9% upside. The firm said the stocks have moved from chaotic, hype‑driven trading to calmer, healthier buying.

Lynx said May and June saw daily volatility nearly double normal levels, driven more by hype than stable strength. Even though Micron's fundamentals looked solid, the stock became "uninvestable" during that high‑volatility stretch. That warning proved accurate. Micron surged 19% in June and then dropped 20% in July.

But August witnessed a major shift. Micron's daily volatility dropped to 3.5%, showing the wild swings from July had cooled. At the same time, the stock quietly climbed 16%, recovering most of its earlier losses. Lynx sees this slow, steady buying as a much stronger base for a real breakout.

Promotion

Improving Memory Market Supports the Thesis

Lynx said the backdrop for memory stocks is getting better. DRAM and NAND spot prices are tightening again as demand for high‑bandwidth memory (HBM) stays strong across AI data centers. With consumer markets stabilizing, Micron's recent strength is seen as a positive signal for peers like SanDisk, Western Digital (WDC), and Seagate (STX).

The firm believes both Micron and SanDisk have now worked through the extremes of optimism and fear, leaving them "primed for a breakout to the upside."

Key Catalysts Next Week

Lynx is watching three clusters of presentations at major tech conferences next week:

  • AI supply chain updates from Nvidia (NVDA), Broadcom (AVGO), and Google (GOOGL) Cloud 
  • Storage demand outlooks from SanDisk, Seagate, and Western Digital 
  • Chip equipment timelines from Lam Research (LRCX), Applied Materials (AMAT), and ASML (ASML)

These updates will help confirm whether memory shortages remain severe and whether demand is still building. If they confirm ongoing AI‑driven memory shortages, Lynx thinks the breakout could happen quickly. On the other hand, any hint of weaker demand or faster capacity expansion could delay it.
